cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Corinth, and he's just spent a whole stretch boasting. Now he says, "I have become a fool, but you drove me to it." That's me standing over an empty cookie box going, "And NOBODY stopped me?"

cards.question: Paul says the Corinthians drove him to act like a fool. What does he say they should have done?

cards.text: Then Paul brings up some people he calls "super-apostles." And he holds himself up right next to them.

cards.question: Paul says he is in no way inferior to those super-apostles.

cards.text: Then he adds, "even though I am nothing." Next he points to proof the Corinthians saw for themselves: the marks of a true apostle, performed right among them with great perseverance.

cards.question: Which marks of a true apostle does Paul say were performed among the Corinthians?

cards.text: Then Paul asks them a question. In what way were they inferior to the other churches?

cards.question: Paul asks how the Corinthians were worse off than the other churches. What's the one exception he names?

answers.text: He was not a burden to them
He sent no helpers to them

cards.text: Then he says, "Forgive me this wrong!" I think he's having a little fun here. That's like apologizing to your neighbor for shoveling his driveway.

cards.question: Paul says he's ready to come to the Corinthians a third time, and he still won't be a burden. Why not?

answers.text: He wants them and not their things
He has plenty of money saved up
Titus will cover all his costs

cards.text: Then Paul explains it with a picture straight out of family life.

cards.question: Paul says children should not have to save up for their ___, but parents for their ___.

cards.text: Now THAT I get. Six kids, and I'd hand over every chocolate chip in this bakery. And Paul says for the sake of their souls, he'll spend his money.

cards.question: For the sake of the Corinthians' souls, Paul will spend his money. What else does he say he'll spend?
Paul says he'll spend for the Corinthians, but only grudgingly.

cards.text: Then Paul asks them, "If I love you more, will you love me less?" Oof. That's the friend who helped you move three times asking why he didn't get invited to the housewarming.
Paul's still on the subject of money. He says, "Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you; but crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery." Then he asks, "Did I exploit you by anyone I sent you?"

cards.question: Paul asks if he exploited the Corinthians through anyone he sent. Then he names someone he urged to visit them. Who?
Paul sent Titus to Corinth all by himself.

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Did Titus exploit you in any way?" I bet he already knows the answer. He's not asking. He's ASKING.

cards.question: Paul asks if he and Titus didn't walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps. What's his point?

answers.text: Titus acted just like Paul did

cards.text: Then Paul asks if they've been thinking all along that he's been making a defense to them.

cards.question: Paul says he speaks before God in Christ, and he calls the Corinthians beloved. What is all of this for?

cards.text: Now Paul says what he's afraid of. When he comes, he may not find them the way he wishes.

cards.question: Paul also worries the Corinthians may not find him the way they wish.
Paul says he fears what he might find when he comes to Corinth. Which of these is on his list?

cards.text: His full list is quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance and disorder. Eight of them. Friend, that's not a church, that's a group chat after midnight.
And Paul has one more fear about when he comes again.

cards.question: Paul is afraid that when he comes again, his God will ___ him before the Corinthians.
When Paul comes again, what does he say will grieve him?

answers.text: Many who sinned and have not repented
Many who left for other churches

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The card says Paul has 'just spent a whole stretch boasting.' That fact comes from before this passage (2 Corinthians 11:16-12:10), but the card only cites 2 Corinthians 12:11 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action in the verse. Paul says the Corinthians 'drove' him to act like a fool, meaning they pushed him into it. The cookie box joke is about overdoing it and blaming others because nobody stopped him. The 'nobody stopped me' idea also nudges the baker toward the wrong answer 'Corrected him' on card 2.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup line 'he holds himself up right next to them' already tells the baker that Paul puts himself on the same level as the super-apostles. That gives away the True answer on card 4.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question already contains both answers ('children should not have to save up for their ___, but parents for their ___'), so the baker only has to swap the two words. Card 11 also calls it 'a picture straight out of family life,' which rules out 'teachers' and 'neighbors.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes over the stop: 5 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. Stop 2 has the same 5/2/1 split.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes over the stop again: 5 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank, the same split as stop 1.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card has three beats in three sentences: Paul is still on money, the quote from verse 16, and the question from verse 17. It is not the opening card, so it should be 1 to 2 sentences and no more than two beats.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The card says 'he's been making a defense,' but the BSB says 'we were making a defense.' Changing 'we' to 'he' narrows who the text is talking about. Verse 18 just grouped Paul with Titus and the brother.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says 'Paul says he speaks before God in Christ,' but the BSB says 'We speak before God in Christ.' Changing 'we' to 'he' narrows who the text is talking about.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'That's not a church, that's a group chat after midnight' laughs at the Corinthians and treats Paul's fear as a fact about them. Paul only says he fears there 'may be' these things.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: Card 12 and this question both frame the moment as something Paul is afraid of. That rules out 'honor' and 'reward,' so 'humble' stands out as the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The kinds of sin Paul names in verse 21 (impurity, sexual immorality and debauchery) never show up on any card. The verse 20 list got its own card, but the passage ends without the baker learning what verse 21 says many have not repented of.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Most story cards in this stop are flat and have no voice: card 6 ('Then Paul asks if they've been thinking all along...'), card 8 ('Now Paul says what he's afraid of...') and card 12 ('And Paul has one more fear about when he comes again.'). Only cards 4 and 11 sound like Papa Dorin. Stop 1 cards 3, 7 and 11 have the same problem.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
